analysis.title: Monthly Market Review, October 2026
key_insights: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 3.75-4% on Oct 27-28 with a 10-2 vote. Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favor of a hike. Sesame sees a December hike as very much on the table.

The FOMC statement upgraded activity to 'expanding at a strong pace' from 'a solid pace', kept inflation 'elevated', and dropped the line about a 'timelier return' to 2%. The 'accumulation of more information' will decide the next step.
Chair Warsh declined to give forward guidance and said the 'monetary medicine' is 'starting to work some', with no firm conclusions yet on the path of policy.
September US CPI accelerated to 3.7% y/y headline and 2.6% core, from 3.4% and 2.4% in August. Price pressures broadened beyond gasoline and energy.
September nonfarm payrolls rose only +29k against a consensus of +90k. Sesame reads this as the labor market responding faster to tight policy than prices are.
The 10-year Treasury yield is around 5% (4.93% at Oct 30), down 36bp on the month. The 2-year is 4.59% (-30bp) and the 30-year is 5.31% (-32bp).
Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a 25bp Fed hike at the December FOMC, versus less than 40% a month earlier.

AI and semiconductor stocks sold off in October. Drivers were an FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is $20bn below earlier signals, Oracle trucking natgas to server farms to work around power limits, and Chinese memory maker CXMT closing the technology gap with Micron and SK Hynix.

Meta posted its first cash outflow in over a decade and announced plans to raise capital. Alphabet burned $5.9bn last quarter, its first negative in 22 years as a public company. Both raised doubts about AI capex funding.
Index moves in October: S&P 500 -0.9%, Nasdaq-100 -6.7%, Stoxx 600 +1.9%, SMI +7.1%, Nikkei 225 -5.2%, MSCI EM -8.1%. The losses were concentrated in AI and semiconductors.

S&P 500 sector moves: Semis & Semi Equipment -13.6%, Communication Services -15.2%, Info Tech -6.8%. Energy rose 14.0%, Consumer Staples 11.4%, Utilities 10.1% and Health Care 9.7%. Sesame reads this as profit-taking in crowded 2026 winners.

WTI rose 17.8% to $104.1/bbl and Brent rose 19.3% to $113.4/bbl. Drivers were Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi targets and airports, and a Russian refinery fire at Ryazan.

The IEA expects the oil market to stay in deficit through year-end, with tight middle distillate supply persisting well into 2027. World oil demand falls 2.5mb/d y/y in 4Q26, and supply is projected to drop 5.8mb/d to 100.7mb/d in 2026.
Gold fell 6.8% to about $3,899/oz, its lowest since mid-August, as oil and inflation lifted rate-hike bets.
The dollar index rose 0.4% to a three-month high. EURUSD fell 1.5% on a French bond selloff, USDBRL rose 5.1% after Lula's re-election and USDMXN rose 4.0%.

Credit spreads widened modestly. iTraxx Crossover 5yr is 326bp (+25bp) and CDX HY 5yr is 356bp (+15bp). Moody's severe scenario puts the trailing global HY default rate at 4.5% by year-end and 6.2% by Sep 2027.
The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% on Oct 29 and flagged energy-driven upside inflation risks and downside growth risks. Lagarde announced she will leave her post next February.
French 10-year spread over Germany widened 38bp to +165bp in October.

sector_views.rationale: S&P 500 Semis fell 13.6% in October on AI funding doubts. Sesame frames the move as profit-taking in crowded winners, not an explicit underweight call.
S&P 500 Energy rose 14.0% in October on higher crude. The report describes the move and gives no rating.
Staples +11.4%, Utilities +10.1% and Health Care +9.7% outperformed in the US. The report describes the move and gives no rating.

earnings_insights: Meta posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade, reported in October earnings, driven by AI-related spending. It announced plans to raise capital.
Alphabet burned $5.9bn last quarter, its first negative cash figure in 22 years as a public company, as it expanded cloud capacity and funded AI development.
Marvell raised guidance and the AMD CEO said chip demand is likely to stay 'very high' for the next several years. Both supported stocks early in October, before the AI selloff.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 3.4% in August, above expectations. Gasoline drove it, and pressures broadened beyond energy.
Up from 2.4% in August. Supports the case for further Fed tightening.
Well below the +90k consensus. Suggests employers are cautious about hiring amid rising costs.
Held on Oct 27-28 by a 10-2 vote, with two dissents for a hike.
Market pricing, up from under 40% a month earlier.
Held on Oct 29. Main refi rate is 2.65% and marginal lending rate is 2.90%.
A surprise draw against a consensus of +15k.
Survey figure for the Nov 2 release. Prior was 54.5.
Survey figure for the Nov 6 release. Prior was 29k.
Demand is falling, yet the IEA still sees balances in deficit through year-end because supply falls faster.

risk_factors: A December Fed hike, which Sesame sees as very much on the table, with a 10-2 vote showing part of the committee wanted a hike now.
A further oil spike from Hormuz tanker attacks, Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure or a possible Iran strike.
Further doubts over AI capex funding and revenue, hitting the concentrated AI and semiconductor winners.
Political and fiscal risk in Europe, especially French bond yields.
Bifurcated credit conditions, with weaker issuers exposed to refinancing pressure and volatility.
EM currency weakness from high oil prices and elevated US yields, including carry-trade unwinds in Mexico.
vol_and_positioning: VIX closed October at 19.42, up 3.1 points on the month. VSTOXX closed at 22.09, up 4.0 points.
The AI selloff is read as profit-taking in this year's crowded winners.
Iron ore (Dalian) fell 4.2% on oversupply and weak demand from loss-making Chinese steel mills.
geopolitical: Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi targets and airports over several days.
Reports said the White House asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterms.
Israeli reports suggested Iran may be preparing a pre-emptive strike after unusual military movements.
A meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, was being weighed by investors.
A major refinery in Ryazan, Russia caught fire, and Ukraine pledged to resume hitting Russian crude-processing facilities.
France proposed that European countries and IEA members release 100mb of diesel and crude.
Trump signaled a cooler appetite to ban US diesel exports.
French government bonds slumped after a weekend of violent unrest and rising US-Ukraine tensions over the war with Russia.
Lula's surprise re-election in Brazil raised fiscal concerns, and USMCA negotiations have stalled.

tension_points.bull_case: Payrolls of +29k against +90k consensus suggest policy is slowing the labor market, which could allow the Fed to delay further hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: CPI accelerated to 3.7% with pressures broadening, two FOMC members dissented for a hike, and the statement dropped the 'timelier return' to 2% line. Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a December hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Oct 18 FOMC minutes and the Nov 6 payrolls (survey 55k vs prior 29k) are the next checks on the hike path.

theme_stances.key_argument: A December hike is very much on the table after the hold, dissents and removal of the timelier-return language.
theme_stances.evidence: That leaves a December hike very much on the table

theme_stances.key_argument: Meta and Alphabet cash burn and the OpenAI revenue shortfall made the AI line look expensive to fund.
